item.text:
<linkedin_post>Google’s plan for an orbital data center depends on satellites being able to share computing work over high-speed optical links. Its first Suncatcher prototype is now online, with two more satellites planned for 2027 to test those links if the current hardware performs well.

The prototype has four Google TPUs and generates up to 1 kW of electricity. Its power supply permits one chip to run at a time for about 20 minutes, adding a constraint to communication with the ground.

Engineers will also test how the chips withstand heat and radiation. A radiation-induced bit flip can corrupt data without triggering normal monitoring tools, so the team will compare performance in orbit with what it observed in ground tests.</linkedin_post>
